entries.note: Links to other sites open in a new tab on published pages with nothing to set; target="_self" keeps a link mark in the same tab; page blocks get real default spacing with a site-wide setting.
behavior: An absolute http or https link to a host other than the site's own now publishes target="_blank" and rel with noopener noreferrer added, with nothing to set. This covers link marks in page text and tables, inline facts, and the links of feature-grid, image-row, card-grid, product-grid, hero-section, cta, image-banner and social-links components, and the footer. mailto and tel links, relative paths, fragments, queries and the site's own addresses (including www.) stay in the same tab; a subdomain counts as another host. Component links have no setting to keep them in the tab.

A link mark keeps its own choice: target="_blank" opens a new tab for any link, and target="_self" keeps even an external link in the same tab. In Markdown write {target="_self"} after the link; in .pm.json set attrs.target to "_self". A mark with a null target, or with the editor's old default rel, follows the default. See help page free-form.

Header navigation follows the same rule: an item or linked group with an http or https address on another host opens in a new tab. mailto and tel items, page items and the site's own addresses stay in the same tab.
A link that opens a new tab now says "(opens in a new tab)" to a screen reader, with no change on screen. This covers component links, link marks, navigation and the footer.
Help for component links and the image-row and product-grid notes no longer say links open in the same tab.
Existing pages change at the site's next whole-site render, such as a settings or navigation change. Pages an incremental publish copies forward keep their old links until then.

Page blocks get real default spacing. Text, tables and every component sit one gap apart, where components used to have no space from the text before them; the last text block of a padded section gets the same gap as room before the section ends; a heading's top margin scales with it. Banners stay flush with their neighbors.

New required setting blockSpacing in settings/taproot-styles.json (Brand & style > Block spacing): compact, standard or roomy scales the gap to 0.75, 1 or 1.5 times, in both color schemes. Standard keeps text where it is today.
spacer blocks add their height to the new gap instead of replacing it, so review hand-placed spacers and remove the ones that only worked around tight spacing.

blockSpacing is required on theme push like every other appearance field. A workspace pulled before this version does not hold it: run pull again before theme push, or add "blockSpacing": "standard" to settings/taproot-styles.json.
A site shows the new spacing after its next whole-site render, such as a settings or navigation change. Pages an incremental publish copies forward keep their old spacing until then.

A section decoration can be sized by height. Set blockSizePercent (an integer from 10 to 200) for "auto N%" in place of inlineSizePercent; the two cannot be combined, and neither set keeps the width default of 40. See help page free-form.
The help reference version is 51.

entries.note: Image defaults can be listed, read and changed safely through media images; metadata advice uses consistent title and description guidance.
behavior: New verbs: media images list [--missing-description] [--page-size <1-100>] [--page-token <cursor>], media images get <image-id>, and media images describe <image-id> --description <text> (or --clear) --expected-revision <n> [--if-missing]. List returns one bounded page and its nextPageToken; the server filters missing defaults before pagination, without scanning page placements or fetching every image separately.

Get/list/describe report stable imageId, uploadedName, nullable defaultDescription, descriptionRevision as an exact decimal string, dimensions, processing state and validated preview URLs. Preview URLs are for inspection and may expire; they are omitted from GitHub Actions output and never written into a description or workspace manifest.

Description writes require the selected site's media permission and the expected revision from list/get. --if-missing is checked atomically by the server and cannot be combined with --clear or blank text. A stale revision or existing default is a refusal, with no automatic overwrite or mutation retry. The server trims outer whitespace, clears blank descriptions to null, and rejects more than 1000 Unicode scalar values without truncation. Existing published output keeps its frozen text until deployment; custom/decorative placement choices stay independent.

Local metadata advice checks known author-entered values consistently: a nonempty title outside 15–70 Unicode scalar values, a description outside 50–160, missing text, or a description matching the title after whitespace and case normalization. Warnings do not block saves. Fallback-dependent metadata remains deferred to the deployment evaluator.

The coordinated release replaces local a11y.image_alt_missing placement advice with a11y.image_default_missing in the stored deployment report. Completeness uses only the frozen image-owned default: contextual alt text, album captions and decorative choices do not waive a missing reusable description. status reads the report and never scans current drafts or triggers compilation.

Image Row and Product Grid image records now follow the shared description contract: descriptionMode selects inherit, custom or decorative, while defaultDescription and descriptionRevision are read-only hydrated metadata and are omitted from authored workspace sources. An Image Row image with descriptionMode inherit may omit alt locally, but its description must resolve to non-blank alt text before deployment; custom and legacy Image Row alt text remains required. See help component image-row and help component product-grid.
The help reference version is 50. Taproot accepts only this latest CLI after the API deploy; upgrade with npm install -g @taprootio/site-authoring@latest.

entries.note: A card-grid can show each card's image whole at a set height, aligned and unframed, with chosen space on any side of the image, so a logo no longer needs a wide padded file.
behavior: A card-grid takes imageFit (cover, the default, or contain), imageHeight (small 2.5rem/40px, medium 4rem/64px, large 6rem/96px at a 16px root), imageAlign (start, center or end) and imageSpacing (an object with any of top, bottom, start and end, each none, small, medium or text). With contain the whole image shows at imageHeight, never cropped or framed, and an image wider than its card shrinks to fit; each card image needs a nonzero width and height, which media upload records. imageHeight and imageAlign are refused unless imageFit is contain. A side left out of imageSpacing keeps its default for the fit: cover has none on every side; contain has small above, none below and text (the padding around the card's text) at start and end. See help component card-grid.
A card-grid image now sits flush with the top of its card, because the article image margin no longer reaches it. A site gets this on its next publish.
The help reference version is 49.

entries.note: Pages gain an image-row component for linked pictures at a set height and a product-grid component for priced cards with a button each; feature-grid help states its icon sizes and square crop, and published feature-grid icons now render at the documented sizes.
behavior: A free-form page may hold an image-row component: one to twelve pictures at one height (small 2.5rem/40px, medium 4rem/64px, large 6rem/96px at a 16px root), each with required alt text, required width and height, and an optional link. Pictures keep their own shape, are never cropped or framed, and one wider than the row shrinks to fit. See help component image-row.

help component feature-grid states the icon box sizes (small 3rem/48px, medium 6rem/96px, large 10rem/160px, xlarge 16rem/256px at a 16px root) and that icons are cropped to a square and framed by the site's image border. Published feature-grid icons now render at those sizes; before this release they filled the item's width with a 2em margin, so re-check existing grids after the runtime update.

A free-form page may hold a product-grid component: one to a hundred equal-height cards for things to buy or book, each with a title, free-text price and note, badge, description, up to eight feature lines, an optional 16:9 image and one button that links to any checkout; columns 2 to 4, standard or compact density, a border width, and a highlighted card drawn in the site's action color. Site checks now read buttonUrl and linkUrl addresses, so a card-grid, cta or product-grid link to a missing page is reported. See help component product-grid.

A free-form page may hold a social-links component: one to twelve links, each a platform from a fixed list (Instagram, Facebook, Yelp, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Pinterest, or Website for any other site) with an https address and an optional label the link reads to screen readers; icons at small 1.5rem, medium 2rem or large 3rem, aligned start, center or end (the align field), with labels shown or hidden. The address must be absolute https, without credentials, to a domain of unaccented letters, digits and hyphens. See help component social-links.

Footer settings gain socialLinks: up to twelve links with an id, a platform key, an https address and an optional label, published as an icon row between the bottom copy and the utility links. The footer draft hash moves to footer-draft-v4, so every footer draft hash issued before this release is stale once: pull the footer again before pushing it. See help footer.
The help reference version is 48.

entries.note: Taproot no longer generates /places, year and month, or tag pages, so a generated page's data drops those fields. One /published page lists every month, a folder page reaches search only with an introduction or three cards, and a review's location byline opens Google Maps.
behavior: The /published/<year> and /published/<year>/<month> pages are no longer generated. One /published page carries a year and a month picker filled from JSON files the release writes (published/months.json and published/<year>/<month>.json), and a content byline links to /published?year=YYYY&month=M. Those file paths are refused as redirect sources with redirect.source_generated_file.

A generated page's data drops year and month beside the place fields: pull writes kind and the four authored fields, and a source that still carries year or month is refused by pages push with pages.document_shape as an unsupported field: delete the year and month lines from sources pulled before this release (every generated page pulled earlier carries year: 0 and month: 0).

The /places index, country, region, city and category pages are no longer generated, so a site has no generated page of those kinds to pull. On a published review, article or album with a place on a site with no map page, the location byline opens the place's Google Maps listing in a new tab; the review's category byline is plain text.

A generated page's data holds kind and the four authored fields. pull no longer writes countryCode, regionCode, citySlug or categorySlug, and a source that still carries one is refused by pages push with pages.document_shape as an unsupported field: delete the four lines from sources pulled before this release.
/places is no longer a reserved path, so a page may be authored there.

A workspace that pulled a /places page before this release keeps that file: pages push reports it as the source of a generated page Taproot no longer publishes and sends the rest, whether or not the site has synchronized the page away yet; naming its path is refused with pages.generated_create. Delete the file.

Taproot no longer generates tag pages (/tags and /tags/<slug>): tags stay page metadata with no public page, a workspace that pulled one keeps the file and pages push reports it as the source of a page Taproot no longer publishes, and /tags is no longer a reserved path. A generated page's data holds kind and the four authored fields; tagId leaves the identity, and a source that still carries it is refused by pages push with pages.document_shape as an unsupported field: delete the line from sources pulled before this release.

A folder index is a search destination when it has an introduction or renders at least three cards; otherwise it carries noindex and leaves the sitemap. Write the page's introductionBody in its pulled .pm.json source to make a small folder one.

Taproot generates a /map page for a site with a public post that has a location. It is a new generated kind in pulls, /map and every path under it are reserved, and /map/places.json cannot be a redirect source.
The help reference version is 47.

entries.note: The site checks refuse a page or redirect source named like a search-engine key file, which the platform now publishes at the site root.
behavior: A redirect source whose first segment is 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters followed by .txt (any capitals, with or without a path beneath it) is refused with redirect.source_generated_file, like sitemap.xml and robots.txt. Taproot writes a file with that name at the root of a site that tells search engines about its releases, so nothing else can sit there. No command changed.
The help reference version is 45.

entries.note: Embedded forms inherit configurable background, border and shadow defaults from the site, with per-form overrides.
behavior: Form definitions accept sparse presentation.background, presentation.border and presentation.shadow boolean overrides. Omitted values inherit the site; explicit false disables the decoration. An empty presentation object is omitted by the form editor.

Site publishing preferences expose formBoxBackground, formBoxBorder and formBoxShadow. Background and shadow default on; border defaults off. Stage publishing preferences and the form version to apply appearance changes.
Forms pull and push preserve appearance overrides, including explicit false.
The help reference version is 44.

entries.note: marketing pull and marketing push keep a site's campaigns and placements as files, and link build prints a tracked address, so an agent can run a site's attribution over the CLI.
behavior: New verbs: taproot-site marketing pull, marketing push [--archive] and link build --path <page> --source <key> [--campaign <key>] [--placement <key>] [--domain <host>]. A key now carries the permissions they need: delegation.content includes site.analytics.view, so a credential minted before this release gains read access to the site's campaigns and placements and, with the publish permission it already held, may change them.

marketing pull writes marketing/campaigns.json and marketing/placements.json (key, name, a campaign's note, starts_on and ends_on, and the read-only state and counted_from) and records a baseline in the pull manifest; a plain pull carries it forward. marketing push validates both files, compares every record with the site, and creates a new key, updates the labels of an existing one, or restores an archived key the file names. A key is public and never changes, so a changed key is a new record; a record the file leaves out is archived only with --archive, and only if the workspace pulled it. A record that changed on the site since the pull is refused (marketing.concurrent_modification, marketing.pull_required). Quota and key refusals are shown as Taproot returns them. There is no plan or apply step, as with forms push.

link build prints one address and saves nothing, with the Marketing link builder's own rules: the source decides the medium, the reader source is not offered, a utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign or utm_content on the path is replaced, and a campaign or placement is checked against marketing/*.json when the workspace has it, otherwise against the site. One that is not live yet is allowed with the builder's note that page views count under the source only until it is. The host is the signed-in site's public address; pass --domain when only a site credential is available.
whoami reports whether the last exchange allows campaigns and placements (marketing.access).
The help reference version is 43.
Built against Espalier 6.7.0. The default site theme is rebuilt against it and its content is unchanged except for the recorded Espalier version, so pulled and validated themes behave as before.

entries.note: Redirects from /s/ addresses are ordinary redirects now that tracked share links are retired.
behavior: A redirect whose source is /s/<anything> saves and validates like any other source. The redirect.source_share_link site-check rule is gone, so offline checks and the server no longer refuse it.

entries.note: Site-specific consent enables legal draft authoring through JSON; legal approval and publication remain in the app.
behavior: Select a standard site, then run login --legal-drafts and approve the pinned site grant in the app. It lasts at most 24 hours and is separate from ordinary account login. Use the global --legal-drafts option before pull, pages push, plan or apply to select that grant.

Pull includes legal bodies as .pm.json with ordinary Content read access. Legal create and update accept JSON only; document key, role and path are immutable, and version, effective date and superseded version are assigned by publication. A changed or new legal draft needs the explicit grant before writes begin.
TAPROOT_SITE_KEY takes precedence; legal writes with an unclassified environment key are refused. Legal approval, deletion and deployment remain app-only. Saving a draft does not approve it.
The help reference version is 42.

entries.note: Image uploads support Taproot’s single-use upload gateway and send an operation key with each upload request.
behavior: media upload sends an operation key when requesting an image upload. It accepts a single-use gateway capability only for the configured Taproot API origin and image-upload path, and never automatically retries that capability after a transport failure or retryable response. Direct signed object-store uploads retain their existing retry behavior.

entries.note: theme resolve prints the colors Espalier compiles from the theme, per scheme and context, with their contrast ratios, offline; the help and the staging review result say how long a review lasts and what ends it; pages delete with a dry run; nav push fenced by a navigation revision.
behavior: New verb: taproot-site theme resolve [--scheme light|dark] [--context <name>] [--site] [--json]. It reads the pulled settings/taproot-styles.json with no credential and no network (--site reads the site's stored theme instead and needs a sign-in), compiles it through Espalier's own pipeline, and prints for the root page and every context in each scheme every semantic color as oklch and hex, whether it is compiled from the roles or pinned (origin compiled, pinned or inherited_pin), and the WCAG contrast of every ink-on-surface pair Espalier defines beside the APCA Lc and its target.

A pair under WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI) is listed in flags with the stable code theme.contrast_text_below_aa and the theme field to edit; flags never refuse, so the exit code is 0. An invalid or incomplete theme is refused with the code theme push and validate use (theme.settings_missing lists every absent path). Without --json the output is a table; with it, the stable result (schemes[].surfaces[].tokens and pairs, contrast, flags). A result too large for the output bound names what it left out in omittedSurfaces (items, count, truncated); --scheme and --context fetch it.
The help reference version is 41.

staging review, deploy and the delivery, preview, redirects and walkthrough help now state that a review handoff works once and expires after two minutes, that opening it starts a five-minute review session that never renews, that the staging site then redirects to the Taproot sign-in (a reviewer without a Taproot account that can preview the site needs a fresh link), and that minting another handoff with the same key (staging review, deploy --staging, redirects check, delivery check --staging) ends the earlier link and any session opened from it. The same text is in stagingPreview.review for staging review and for deploy --staging --handoff on a managed Docs site. No command or refusal changed.

Correction to 0.22.4: analyticsConsentPrompt is read-only in the CLI. A pull records it in the publishing preferences, but no push verb writes it (theme push writes only the appearance scalars, both themes and the footer colours); switch it on or off in the app under Settings, then deploy. help settings has said so since 0.22.4.

pages delete <path> [--dry-run] deletes one tracked page and removes its source and manifest entry, so a test page no longer needs the app. It runs the same revision fence as pages push first (pages.push_conflict, nothing deleted), refuses a page navigation, the footer or a form's after-submit page still uses (pages.delete_referenced, naming each use), reports redirects that land on the page in redirectsToPage, and stages the removal of a page the live site serves (effect removalStaged): the page stays live until a deployment promotes the removal, so deploy --staging then deploy finish the job, and pull, push, plan and approve treat it as deleted. The home page, 404, generated, legal and integration-managed pages are refused. A page the site already deleted or staged for removal is only cleaned from the workspace (effect alreadyDeleted or alreadyRemovalStaged).

pull records the navigation revision beside the tree (navigation.revision in the manifest and in pull's result), and nav push presents it. A tree edited in the app since the pull is refused with nav.concurrent_modification and nothing is written; keep a copy of nav.json, run pull, re-apply the edits and push again. A manifest with no navigation revision (a workspace pulled by an earlier release) is refused with nav.pull_required: run pull once. A successful push records the revision it saved, so the next push is fenced against it, and a push whose answer was lost after it committed is settled by running it again (navigation.alreadyApplied, nothing sent). The result no longer carries lastWriteWins; navigation.revision is the saved revision.

entries.note: The publishing preferences gain analyticsConsentPrompt, the switch that asks readers before the visit cookie is set.
behavior: A pulled settings snapshot now carries analyticsConsentPrompt (default false) in the publishing preferences, and a push can set it. It is staged like the rest of the group and applies after a deployment. With it on, published pages show a small prompt and the 30-minute visit cookie is set only after a reader accepts.

entries.note: The forms reference now says site moderators can read form submissions.
behavior: The forms help names who holds the submissions permissions: site.forms.submissions.read belongs to a site's owners, admins and moderators, and site.forms.submissions.manage to its owners and admins. No command or refusal changed.

entries.note: Free-form sections pad evenly with the page padding wherever they render, including preview-page; Espalier 6.5.0 lets the page preview take the width a capped main column leaves it.
behavior: The renderer writes a standard free-form section's padding on the section (--esp-size-padding on every side, in place of Espalier's side padding of --esp-size-medium and larger top and bottom), so preview-page and the editor's live preview show the same padding the published page does. A section with no theme context also shows the page background through it, as the published page does. Sections with contentPadding none are unchanged. Republish to apply it to a published page.

Espalier 6.5.0 changes the editor page layout only. The default site theme is rebuilt against it and its content is unchanged except for the recorded Espalier version, so pulled and validated themes behave as before.

entries.note: Espalier 6.4.0: dialogs can be bounded by inset properties; the default site theme output is unchanged.
behavior: Espalier 6.4.0 adds four inset properties on dialogs and lets a full-screen box follow them. The default site theme is rebuilt against it and its content is unchanged except for the recorded Espalier version, so pulled and validated themes behave as before.

entries.note: validate warns when a free-form page has no h1 or a banner or hero already claims it, and about alt text, link text, long titles and missing descriptions.
behavior: validate reports page-structure warnings in findings, never refusing: seo.h1_missing for a free-form page with no # heading, banner title or hero title; seo.h1_demoted when a # heading publishes as an h2 because the banner's overlay text, a hero title or an earlier # heading is already the h1 (detail names which); seo.h1_multiple for a hero title after the h1; seo.heading_renumbered and seo.heading_before_title for headings published at another level; a11y.image_alt_missing; a11y.link_text_empty. Any page gets seo.title_long and seo.description_missing.
validate's siteChecks gains checkedInEditor, the rules only the page editor evaluates (a cover, a description field, or a description's length, which descriptionWarnings reports here).

The API refuses a page save that newly places a form that does not exist or is archived, and a first form block on a Profile or Docs site, with a validation error on Forms; status lists form.not_supported_on_site_type among the site findings. preview-page now renders the form a page places, from its current version.

validate refuses a component:form formKey that none of the workspace's forms/<key>.json files has (pages.form_unknown, rule form.key_unknown), naming the file it expected; a workspace with no forms/ directory is not checked. pages push and plan say whether the missing key's file is in the workspace.

pull writes a stored light or dark theme as the generator renders it: as stored over Espalier's defaults alone. It no longer layers the Taproot house theme under a theme the CLI does not manage, so a sparse theme from such a site pulls with Espalier's values for the keys it never set, so the pulled theme matches what the published site renders.

entries.note: Review URLs stay out of deploy output unless you ask; deploy --staging waits until staging serves the new release; validate reports site checks; help corrections for free-form h1, legal pages, settings and logos; this changelog.
behavior: deploy --staging and redirects check no longer report a live single-use review URL: stagingPreview.url is empty and stagingPreview.reason is staging.handoff_not_requested. Pass --handoff for a fresh URL in the result, or run staging review. --no-handoff states the default.

staging review takes --path <page> to open the review on that page instead of the home page; deploy --staging --handoff and redirects check --handoff take --review-path <page>. The path is checked offline (staging.review_path_invalid).

pull and nav push write nav.json without default-only fields (no empty externalUrl, resourceId or children), and nav push rewrites nav.json from the saved tree after a successful save; either form is accepted.
Footer text runs omit bold, italic and underline when they are false, in pull and footer push; either form is accepted.

New command: changelog [--since <version>] prints these notes offline, and status reports the installed version's note. The cli_outdated refusal now carries latestVersion and the changelog command to run after upgrading.

deploy --staging on a Standard site waits, bounded at 180 seconds, until staging serves the new release before it finishes, and reports stagingServed as served, propagating or unverified; the result never fails on the wait. Propagation can take up to about 120 seconds after the deployment completes.

validate runs the shared site check rules it can run offline and reports findings (ruleId, severity, pageId, subject) and siteChecks (ranOffline, checkedBySite, checkedAtDeploy); redirect refusals keep their codes and carry the rule id. status reads the site health summary; the broken-references report is gone, so an older CLI needs this upgrade.
Published forms mark required fields with an asterisk and a legend; help forms describes the mark.

Help corrections: a free-form page renders no automatic heading and its first level-1 heading is the h1; help pages lists the read-only legal page type and help page legal describes it; the new help settings topic maps every pulled setting to the app control that writes it and says where it renders; logo.png and logo@2x.png are not paired, so assign the highest-resolution file.
Espalier 6.3.0: a field fills one layer above the surface that contains it; the default site theme was rebuilt for it.

entries.note: Pages place a form by its id, so renaming a form never breaks a page; form names are unique on a site.
behavior: pages push turns a component:form formKey into the form's id, and refuses a key the site does not have (pages.form_unknown) or has archived (pages.form_archived) before writing anything; plan reports the same. pages pull writes the key back, and keeps an id the site no longer has.
forms validate and forms push refuse two forms with the same name, ignoring case (forms.name_duplicate, forms.name_taken).

The first pages pull after the server release can report pages.pull_conflict for a Markdown page that places a form, though its content is the same; run pages push for that page, or delete the file and pull again.

entries.note: Forms can email the site owner an hourly count of new submissions, and a newsletter sink needs a consent checkbox.
behavior: A form file takes an optional top-level notify_owner boolean. New forms default to false, omitting it on an existing form keeps the site's choice, and it takes effect without a new version or publishing.
A newsletter sink requires a required email contact field and at least one consent checkbox, and every consent checkbox must be checked.
forms.concurrent_modification is also raised when the site's operational settings moved since the last read.

entries.note: Place categories can be set per site, and deploy shows the pages it will generate before it sends anything.
behavior: New commands: places category list, places category set <placeId> <category> and places category clear <placeId> change the category this site files a place review under.

deploy --staging plans the candidate first and reports the pages it will generate and the allowance left (readiness.pageEstimate); a candidate that does not fit stops with deploy.page_allowance_exceeded before anything is sent.
A deploy refused for the pages-generated allowance or the bandwidth pause reports plan_limit with the time it can lift.
